label: Why total IT jobs hold while their employer changes
story: AI raises output per worker, so fewer staff are needed for the same work. Work that moves to a GCC still needs people, so the GCC hires as the vendor shrinks. At the same time GCCs win work from vendors and their scale advantage feeds itself, so total IT staff moves less than the split between employers.

label: Staffing catches up with the work
The GCC scale loop
story: The more IT work GCCs hold, the stronger their scale advantage, and the more clients choose them; the work they take comes out of vendors' books, and GCC hiring from vendors raises their costs. The advantage is capped: the loop feeds back until about 2032, then sits at its cap, a fixed shift with no further gain.

story: A vendor whose margin falls well below normal loses clients and cuts staff; lost clients cut its revenue and margin further. Over time clients get used to the distress, so the flight fades.
